IRS990.MissionDesc: VILLAGE ENTERPRISE'S MISSION IS TO END EXTREME POVERTY IN RURAL AFRICA THROUGH ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND INNOVATION. PARTNERING WITH GOVERNMENTS, NONPROFITS, UNITED NATIONS AGENCIES, CONSERVATION ORGANIZATIONS, AND PRIVATE SECTOR COMPANIES, (SEE SCHEDULE O)
IRS990.Desc: THE DELIVERING RESILIENT ENTERPRISES AND MARKET SYSTEMS (DREAMS) PROJECT PROVIDES INNOVATIVE SOLUTION THAT DRIVES REFUGEE SELF-RELIANCE. THE PROJECT IS COFUNDED BY FIVE FOUNDATIONS AND IT AIMS TO PROVIDE TWO HUNDRED THOUSAND OF THE MOST VULNERABLE REFUGEES IN UGANDA AND ETHIOPIA.

ProgSrvcAccomActy2Grp.Desc: CATHOLIC RELIEF SERVICES (CRS)-NAWIRI - CRS AND THE CONSORTIUM THAT VILLAGE ENTERPRISE FUND IS A MEMBER OF WERE AWARDED A FEDERAL COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT FROM USAID TO IMPLEMENT THE USAID MFUMO IMARA LISHE ENDELEVU (MILE) PROGRAM IN DELIVERING A MULTISECTORAL PACKAGE OF SERVICES TO SUPPORT LOCAL INSTITUTIONS TO SUSTAINABLY REDUCE PERSISTENT ACUTE MALNUTRITION AMONG VULNERABLE SUBPOPULATIONS OF ISIOLO AND MARSABIT COUNTIES IN KENYA. VILLAGE ENTERPRISE LEADS A POVERTY GRADUATION PROGRAM BY BUILDING ON ITS ENTREPRENEURIAL FOUNDATION THAT HAS SUPPORTED NEW ENTERPRISES IN KENYA.

ProgSrvcAccomActy3Grp.Desc: VILLAGE ENTERPRISE FUND WAS AWARDED A FEDERAL COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT FROM USAID TO IMPLEMENT THE USAID SCALING SUSTAINABLE POVERTY GRADUATION PROGRAM IN RWANDA. THE PROGRAM SUPPORTS FIRST-TIME ENTREPRENEURS IN MOVING BEYOND EXTREME POVERTY BY EQUIPPING THEM WITH THE RESOURCES, KNOWLEDGE, AND LEADERSHIP SKILLS NEEDED TO START SUSTAINABLE BUSINESSES AND SAVINGS GROUPS. THROUGH THIS PROGRAM, VILLAGE ENTERPRISE AIMS TO EXPONENTIALLY SCALE ITS COST-EFFECTIVE, INNOVATIVE, AND EVIDENCE-BASED GRADUATION APPROACH, BOTH BY EXPANDING DIRECT IMPLEMENTATION IN RWANDA AND BY FOSTERING REPLICATION AND ADOPTION OF THE MODEL BY THE GOVERNMENT OF RWANDA AND OTHER AFRICAN COUNTRIES. THE GOAL IS TO REACH 10 MILLION BENEFICIARIES WITHIN TEN YEARS.

ProgSrvcAccomActyOtherGrp.Desc: THE BILL & MELINDA GATES FOUNDATION SUPPORTED PROGRAM STRENGTHENED THE SCALABILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY OF VILLAGE ENTERPRISE'S ULTRA-POOR GRADUATION (UPG) MODEL IN KENYA THROUGH GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE SECTOR INTEGRATION. THE PROGRAM ADVANCED PARTNERSHIPS WITH COUNTY GOVERNMENTS BY SUPPORTING POLICY DEVELOPMENT, BUILDING INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY, AND IMPLEMENTING MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEMS TO ENABLE LOCAL OWNERSHIP AND DELIVERY OF POVERTY GRADUATION PROGRAMS. IN ADDITION, THE INITIATIVE PILOTED AN INNOVATIVE APPROACH THAT INTEGRATES UPG WITH MARKET SYSTEMS DEVELOPMENT, LINKING PARTICIPANTS TO PRIVATE SECTOR ACTORS AND VALUE CHAINS TO STRENGTHEN THE GROWTH AND SUSTAINABILITY OF MICROENTERPRISES. THE PROGRAM ALSO GENERATED LEARNING TO INFORM NATIONAL-LEVEL SOCIAL PROTECTION PROGRAMS AND CONTRIBUTE TO THE EVOLUTION OF ECONOMIC INCLUSION STRATEGIES IN KENYA.

THE GREATER IMPACT FOUNDATION (GIF) PROJECT SUPPORTED THE EXPANSION OF VILLAGE ENTERPRISE'S RURAL MICROENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM IN KENYA AND UGANDA. THE PROGRAM DELIVERED ENTREPRENEURSHIP TRAINING, SEED CAPITAL, AND BUSINESS MENTORSHIP TO VULNERABLE HOUSEHOLDS IN WEST POKOT AND MT. ELGON (KENYA), AND GULU AND SOROTI (UGANDA), ENABLING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW MICROENTERPRISES AND STRENGTHENING HOUSEHOLD INCOME GENERATION. THE INITIATIVE INCORPORATED PROGRAM EFFICIENCY IMPROVEMENTS TO EXPAND OUTREACH AND COST-EFFECTIVENESS, AND INCLUDED MONITORING OF PREVIOUSLY SUPPORTED BUSINESSES TO INFORM LEARNING AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT OF THE MODEL.

SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: VEF EMPLOYEES VISIT THE FIELD SITES REGULARLY TO VERIFY GRANTS MADE DURING THE YEAR AND FOLLOW UP ON THE PROGRESS ACHIEVED BY OUR PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS.

SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: VILLAGE ENTERPRISE MONITORS ITS SUBAWARDS THROUGH A COMBINATION OF FORMAL SUBAWARD AGREEMENTS, PERIODIC PROGRAMMATIC AND FINANCIAL REPORTING, BUDGET MONITORING, AND ONGOING COMMUNICATION WITH SUBRECIPIENTS. SUBAWARD AGREEMENTS ESTABLISH THE APPROVED SCOPE OF WORK, BUDGET, REPORTING REQUIREMENTS, COMPLIANCE OBLIGATIONS, AUDIT RIGHTS, AND PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS. SUBRECIPIENTS ARE REQUIRED TO SUBMIT PERIODIC NARRATIVE AND FINANCIAL REPORTS, AND VILLAGE ENTERPRISE REVIEWS PROGRESS AGAINST APPROVED ACTIVITIES, DELIVERABLES, TIMELINES, AND BUDGET UTILIZATION. ADDITIONAL MONITORING MAY INCLUDE REQUESTS FOR SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW MEETINGS, AUDITS, EVALUATIONS, AND FOLLOW-UP ON COMPLIANCE OR PERFORMANCE ISSUES AS NEEDED.
BONUSES SHOWN ON PART II ARE CONTRACTUAL BONUSES THAT ARE CONDITIONAL ON MEETING REVENUE TARGETS.
CERTAIN EMPLOYEES RECEIVED A PERFORMANCE BASED BONUS PAYMENT, BASED ON COMPANY PERFORMANCE METRICS AND CONTRACT STIPULATIONS. THE CEO AND PRESIDENT'S BONUS IS AT THE DISCRETION OF THE BOARD.

VILLAGE ENTERPRISE EQUIPS FIRST-TIME ENTREPRENEURS IN AFRICA WITH RESOURCES AND SKILLS TO START CLIMATE-SMART BUSINESSES AND SAVINGS GROUPS. LOCALLY-LED AND COMMUNITY-BASED, THE ORGANIZATION WORKS WITH THE MOST VULNERABLE WOMEN, REFUGEES, AND YOUTH IN RURAL AFRICA AND EQUIP THEM TO ADAPT TO THE SHOCKS OF DROUGHT, DISPLACEMENT, THE PANDEMIC, AND CONFLICT.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION B, LINE 11B
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE FORM 990 DRAFT IS REVIEWED BY THE CFO AND OTHER INTERNAL STAFF. THE DRAFT FILING IS DISTRIBUTED TO THE MEMBERS OF THE GOVERNANCE BODY FOR REVIEW AND THEIR APPROVAL BEFORE THE FINAL COPY IS FILED.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION B, LINE 12C
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE ORGANIZATION HAS A CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY IN PLACE. ALL BOARD MEMBERS OF THE ORGANIZATION AND ITS AFFILIATED ENTITIES ARE REQUIRED TO REIVEW THE POLICY AND DISCLOSE AND CONFLICTS, IN WRITING, WHEN THEY JOIN THE BOARD. MANAGEMENT MONITORS THE POLICY BY DISTRIBUTING CONFLICT OF INTEREST FORMS TO ALL BOARD MEMBERS ANNUALLY. THE BOARD MEMBERS ARE REQUIRED TO REVIEW AND COMPLETE THE FORMS, DISCLOSING ANY CONFLICTS, AND RETURN THEM TO THE STAFF BOARD LIASON WHO MAINTAINS THE RECORDS.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION B, LINE 15
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: COMPARABILITY DATA IS USED TO DETERMINE WHAT PROPER COMPENSATION PACKAGE IS REASONABLE FOR ALL EMPLOYEES. THE BOARD AND OFFICERS DO A THOROUGH ANALYSIS OF POTENTIAL CANDIDATES FOR UPPER MANAGEMENT POSITIONS DETERMINING THE PACKAGE THAT ACKNOWLEDGES THEIR EXPERIENCE AND RESPONSIBILITIES. ANNUAL CHANGES IN COMPENSATION ARE REVIEWED WITH THE HR & GOVERNANCE COMMITTEE PRIOR TO IMPLEMENTATION. DISCUSSIONS AROUND ALL COMPENSATION DECISIONS ARE REFLECTED IN THE COMMITTEE MEETING NOTES. THE LAST REVIEW PROCESS TOOK PLACE IN JUNE 2025.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION C, LINE 19
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY ARE AVAILABLE ON THE ORGANIZATION'S WEBSITE. UPON REQUEST, THE ORGANIZATION WILL MAKE AVAILABLE ONLY THOSE DOCUMENTS REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE PUBLIC INSPECTION LAW.
